Title: Plastic in the Great Lakes
Content: Small pieces of plastic called pellets are a major type of plastic pollution found on the shorelines of the Great Lakes. Pellets are produced and then transported to factories to be melted and formed into plastic products. Pellets are microplastics, meaning they are less than `text(5 millimeters)` in diameter. Unfortunately, pellets are often spilled or released into the environment during production, transport, and storage. Plastic pellets can make their way into drainage systems, circulate through water systems such as the Great Lakes, and eventually be deposited along shorelines.

The Great Lakes contain over `text(one-fifth)` of the world’s fresh water. Humans rely on the water in the Great Lakes for many uses. `text(Seventy-one percent)` of the water withdrawn from the Great Lakes is used for cooling power plants; `text(14 percent)` of the water is used for public water supply. The Great Lakes are also used for irrigation of fields, fishing, transporting cargo, and recreation.

When microplastics are eaten by aquatic animals and shorebirds, the plastics can harm these animals’ health and ability to reproduce. Studies such as the one above can provide information that can be used to guide new laws and regulations to protect the environment from plastic pollution.
